requirements:
2048 mechanics, level 1.

R1. Implement in Rust as a SINGLE source file that compiles with rustc --edition 2024, std only. Output ONLY the Rust source code inside ```rust fences. Do not use inner attributes or inner documentation comments.

R2. The exact public API is:
```rust
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Side { Left, Right }
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Error { RowTooLong { len: usize }, InvalidTile { index: usize, value: u32 }, MergeOverflow { first: usize, second: usize } }
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Merge { pub from: [usize; 2], pub to: usize, pub value: u32 }
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct RowResult { pub cells: Vec<u32>, pub score: u64, pub changed: bool, pub merges: Vec<Merge> }
pub fn slide_row(row: &[u32], side: Side) -> Result<RowResult, Error>;
```

R3. All listed enums/structs implement the shown derives. All indices are zero-based; equality compares all fields.

R4. Rows may have length 0 through 32 inclusive. Longer rows return RowTooLong with the actual length.

R5. A valid cell is 0 (empty) or a power of two from 2 through 2147483648 inclusive. Return InvalidTile for any other value, with its original input index and value.

R6. Error precedence: check row length first, then ALL cells for invalid values in increasing original index, then merging. Thus any invalid tile beats any merge overflow, irrespective of side.

R7. Never modify the input slice. Return owned result cells of exactly the input length.

R8. Discard zeroes for purposes of deciding adjacency; equal tiles separated only by zeroes can merge.

R9. Scan nonempty tiles from the destination edge: increasing original index for Left, decreasing for Right.

R10. Process that scan greedily: two consecutive equal input tiles merge into their sum and are both consumed. A merged output never merges again during this move. Unequal tiles each remain single.

R11. Merging two 2147483648 tiles returns MergeOverflow; do not wrap or saturate.

R12. If multiple merges would overflow, report the first encountered in the scan, with first and second equal to the original indices of that pair in scan order. No partial result is returned.

R13. Pack outputs against the destination edge in scan order and fill all remaining cells with zero.

R14. Each merge produces one Merge whose from contains the two original indices in scan order, even when tiles crossed empty cells.

R15. Merge.to is the final output index after compaction, and Merge.value is the new doubled value.

R16. The merges vector is in encounter order from the destination edge; do not sort it by numeric indices.

R17. score is the u64 sum of the NEW values of all merges, excluding unmerged tiles.

R18. changed is exactly whether returned cells differ from the input, irrespective of score.

R19. A successful unchanged move has score 0 and an empty merges vector. Pure sliding may have changed=true with score 0.

R20. Empty rows succeed unchanged with empty cells; a one-cell valid row succeeds unchanged on either side. There is no target-tile stopping rule.
